Leadership asks for "AI on our data". Every Snowflake AI feature could play a part, and choosing badly means paying for three services where one SQL function would do. This phase builds Brightwell's whole AI estate, one layer at a time, and ends with a capstone that joins them. Choosing a component Copy What you should see Copy Copy The function is deliberately simple, but the questions are the ones that matter in a real design review: what kind of data, who is asking, and what must come back. Notice how often the answer is a SQL function in a pipeline rather than an agent: bulk enrichment is cheaper, testable and explainable, and agents are worth their cost only when the question is open-ended. Why "next to the data" matters Calling an external model from a Python job means exporting data, managing a second set of credentials and copying permissions by hand. In Snowflake, the AI call runs inside the query: role-based access, masking policies and row access policies apply before the model sees a row, usage is attributed to the user and query, and the output lands in a governed table. The trade-offs are real too: you choose from the models Snowflake hosts, inference may need to run in another region (lesson 33.2 ), and costs are in credits that need their own monitoring (lesson 33.18 ). a3302: Course home / Phase 33 · AI on Snowflake, End to End Access, Model RBAC, Cross-Region Inference and Spend Controls Lesson 33.2 60 min Lesson Completed Lesson goals What you will be able to do Grant exactly the privileges a role needs to call AI functions, specific models and agents Decide the cross-region inference setting from data-residency requirements, not by default Put budgets and per-user quotas in place before the first large job Before you start Needs : Lesson 17.25 · LLM Security: Secrets, API Key Rotation, Audit Logs and Guardrails ; Lesson 17.26 · AI Compliance: SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI-DSS, the EU AI Act and ISO 42001 Type : Lesson (setup with code). Time : about an hour. In plain words first The idea in one line Before anyone calls a model, decide who may call which model, where inference may run, and how much they may spend, and write all three down as grants and settings. The problem Brightwell's first AI pilot ran as ACCOUNTADMIN "to save time". It used the largest model for everything, inference silently ran in another region, and the month's AI bill surprised finance. All three are settings, and all three should be decided on day one. Layer 1: may this role use AI functions at all? Calling Cortex AI Functions needs two things: the account-level USE AI FUNCTIONS privilege (or a per-function USE AI FUNCTION <name> privilege) and one of two database roles. SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER covers the AI functions and is also needed for Search, Analyst and Agents. SNOWFLAKE.AI_FUNCTIONS_USER is narrower: scalar AI functions only, so not AI_AGG or AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG , and not Search, Analyst, Agents or fine-tuning. Agents need SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER or SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER , plus privileges on the agent and on every object its tools use. Mind the defaults: USE AI FUNCTIONS and SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER are granted to PUBLIC out of the box, so every role can call AI functions until you revoke them. A governed account revokes both and grants them to named roles. Copy Layer 2: which models? Model access is now role-based. Each Cortex model has an object in SNOWFLAKE.MODELS and an application role CORTEX-MODEL-ROLE-<MODEL> ; CORTEX-MODEL-ROLE-ALL covers every current and future model. The older account parameter CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST is being deprecated: from August 2026 it can only be set to 'None' , and Snowflake recommends moving to RBAC. By default, a bootstrap grant gives all models to PUBLIC ; a careful account revokes it and grants models deliberately. Copy ACCOUNTADMIN always has access, so test grants as the real role. Changes reach the Cortex REST API and AI Gateway within about five minutes. Layer 3: where may inference run? Some models are not hosted in every region. CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION (set only by ACCOUNTADMIN, at account level) decides whether a request may be processed elsewhere. Values: DISABLED ; a region group such as AWS_EU , AWS_US , AZURE_EU ; a cloud such as AWS_GLOBAL ; or ANY_REGION . Stored data stays in the account's region; the prompt and response travel encrypted and are not persisted in the processing region, and there is no egress charge. New organisations created after 9 March 2026 default to ANY_REGION , and other accounts inherit a same-cloud geography, so set it explicitly if you have residency rules. Copy Layer 4: how much may they spend? From the AI cost governance docs: budgets (monthly limits for the account or a group of objects, with notifications and actions; resource budgets for tagged agents, CoWork and Search), shared resource budgets for AI features by tagged users, and per-user quotas , the only AI control with built-in enforcement, covering AI Functions, Cortex Agents, CoCo, AI Gateway and CoWork. Budget actions can lag by hours; quotas act within minutes. A local model of the access check The decision Snowflake makes on each call can be written as a small function. Modelling it is a good way to review a grant design before applying it. Copy What you should see Copy Copy The analyst can classify and complete but not aggregate, because AI_FUNCTIONS_USER excludes the aggregate functions. The store manager cannot call AI functions directly at all, by design: they reach AI only through the agent they were granted. The second line is the residency rule doing its job: the model exists, the role could be granted it, but the account does not allow processing in the US. The answer is a different model, not a looser setting, unless the data owner agrees. (The model availability table here is invented for the exercise; check real availability with SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS .) Check your mental model Which statements are right? ✓ Testing grants as ACCOUNTADMIN proves nothing, because ACCOUNTADMIN always has model access. ✗ CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST is the recommended way to control model access in late 2026. It is being deprecated in favour of model RBAC through application roles. ✓ Per-user quotas are the AI cost control with built-in enforcement. Recap What to keep Function access: USE AI FUNCTIONS (or per function) plus CORTEX_USER or the narrower AI_FUNCTIONS_USER ; revoke the PUBLIC defaults. Model access: application roles per model; revoke the PUBLIC bootstrap grant. Set CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION explicitly; put budgets and per-user quotas in place first. In plain words first The idea in one line Files become usable by AI when they sit on a stage Snowflake can list, are parsed once into text with page structure, and are stored in a table that later steps can chunk, search and extract from. The problem Brightwell's knowledge lives in 3,400 files: return policies (PDF), supplier contracts (PDF and DOCX), product spec sheets (PPTX) and scanned warranty cards (JPEG). Some arrive weekly from SharePoint. Parsing every file on every run is slow and costly; parsing nothing leaves the agents blind. Stages and directory tables Copy TO_FILE('@docs.raw.files', 'policies/returns-2026.pdf') turns a staged path into a FILE reference that AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT , AI_EXTRACT , AI_COMPLETE and AI_TRANSCRIBE accept. For sources such as SharePoint and Google Drive, Openflow connectors sync files incrementally into a stage (the "simple ingest" variants) or straight into a Cortex Search service (the Cortex Search variants), optionally with document permissions. Parsing AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT(file, options) has three modes: 'OCR' (text only), 'LAYOUT' (keeps headings and tables as Markdown) and 'AGENTIC' (adds understanding of charts and diagrams). page_split => TRUE returns one object per page, which you want for citations and chunking. It is billed per page processed, so parse once and keep the result. Copy Client-side encrypted stages also work with AI_EXTRACT and AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT since August 2026. Limits worth designing around: 100 MB per file, up to 2,000 pages per document, and page selection ( page_filter or FL_FILTER_PAGES ) to process only the pages you need, which also limits the bill. Multiply the page counts by the per-page rate in Snowflake's Service Consumption Table to turn this into credits. In plain words first The idea in one line Task functions are purpose-built model calls with fixed outputs; use them for routine enrichment and measure them on labelled data before you rely on them. The problem Brightwell has 4 million product reviews and 300,000 support tickets a year. The product team wants each review tagged by theme, the service team wants English translations of non-English tickets, legal wants personal data removed before anything is shared, and leadership wants "what are customers saying about our tents this quarter?" Which function for which job Function Returns Brightwell use AI_CLASSIFY(input, categories [, config]) {"labels": [...]} (single or multi-label) Review theme: fit, durability, waterproofing, delivery, price AI_FILTER(input) or AI_FILTER(PROMPT(...)) BOOLEAN Keep reviews that mention a safety issue; match tickets to policies AI_SENTIMENT(text) Sentiment, overall and by aspect Track sentiment by product line AI_AGG(expr, instruction) / AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG(expr) One string across many rows, no context-window limit "Top complaints about tents this quarter" AI_TRANSLATE(text, source, target) Translated text Tickets from French and German customers AI_REDACT(text) Text with personal data masked Before sharing tickets with a supplier AI_EXTRACT(text or file, responseFormat) Named fields Lesson 33.6 Copy Locally: evaluate the classifier before trusting it Take 300 reviews labelled by the product team, run AI_CLASSIFY on them, and compare. Copy What you should see Copy Copy Overall accuracy looks fine; the per-class table shows where it is not. fit has the lowest recall: 17 fit reviews were tagged durability , which also drags durability's precision down to 0.80. delivery picks up a few stray fit and price reviews. The fixes are cheap: sharpen the category descriptions, add two or three examples in the config, and re-measure on the same labelled set. Because labels, descriptions and examples are billed on every row, keep them short. The AI_FILTER join trap AI_FILTER can join two tables on a natural-language condition, for example matching tickets to the policy clauses that apply. Every pair is a model call. Copy What you should see Copy Copy Snowflake optimises AI_FILTER queries automatically where it can (reporting 2 to 10 times faster runs and up to 60% fewer tokens), but no optimiser makes 800,000 calls cheap. In plain words first The idea in one line Ask for exactly the fields you need, keep the model's confidence and the page it read from, and send anything uncertain to a person instead of straight into a table. The problem Brightwell's 900 supplier contracts decide what it can claim back when goods are faulty. Finance needs four values from each: supplier name, defect claim window (days), who pays return shipping, and the table of volume discounts. Retyping them took a temp two months last year. AI_EXTRACT AI_EXTRACT takes text or a file and a responseFormat : an object of {label: question} , an array of questions, or a JSON schema that can include lists and tables. Named arguments add scores => TRUE (a 0 to 1 score per field) and citation => TRUE (page and bounding box for documents, character spans for text; citations need cross-region inference). Limits: 100 MB per file; up to 1,000 pages with cross-region inference or 125 without; up to 100 field questions or 10 table questions per call. Copy The result has response (the fields), error , and with scores a scoring object. Each page counts as 970 input tokens for billing, and the response format counts too, so page selection (lesson 33.3 ) matters here as much as for parsing. Locally: measure, threshold and route A finance analyst checked 120 contracts by hand. Compare extraction against them field by field, then choose a score threshold that sends doubtful values to review. Copy What you should see Copy Copy With no threshold, all 34 errors land in the finance table. At 0.70, only 4 get through and 31 values go to a person; at 0.75, none get through in this sample and 43 go to review. Raising it further only adds review work. On real data the curve is never this clean, so measure it rather than assume it. Pick the threshold with the data owner: it is a business trade between review effort and errors, and it differs by field (a wrong supplier name is worse than a wrong discount row that finance will see anyway). Incremental and auditable Copy Keep the full JSON ( x ) in an append-only log table and build the clean table as a view or dynamic table over it, with the score threshold applied there. That way a threshold change does not need re-extraction, and every value can be traced to its run, file and, with citation => TRUE , its page. Creating the service Copy Decisions in that statement: the search column is the chunk text; attributes are the only columns you can filter on; TARGET_LAG sets freshness (and refresh cost); the embedding model cannot be changed later without CREATE OR REPLACE (the default is snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5 , English). A PRIMARY KEY (text columns) enables a cheaper refresh path, and the multi-index form ( TEXT INDEXES , VECTOR INDEXES ) lets you choose which columns are searched by keyword and which by vector, including your own embeddings. Querying Copy Copy Filter operators: @eq , @contains (arrays), @gte and @lte (numbers and dates), @primarykey , combined with @and , @or , @not .
